name: Mesh-Embedded Gaussian Splatting
definition: A hybrid 3D representation where 3D Gaussians are embedded on a canonical triangle mesh (SMPL-X or FLAME) to disentangle motion (mesh) from appearance (Gaussians). The Gaussians are defined by barycentric coordinates and displacement on the mesh, allowing explicit motion control by the mesh without MLP-based linear blend skinning fields.
summary: Mesh-Embedded Gaussian Splatting is a hybrid 3D representation that embeds Gaussians onto a canonical mesh to disentangle motion and appearance, enabling direct compatibility with skeletal animation and mesh editing.
